newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler-Benz to introduce new financing methods.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz to introduce new financing methods.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG, Germany's largest industrial company, said Wednesday it planned to introduce several new innovative financing methods, some in emerging markets.
Daimler Chief Financial Officer Manfred Gentz, addressing a group of bankers, said the company will soon introduce new ways to finance projects in regions with less-developed financial markets.

"In these financing models, managed by an international bank, local investors will present capital which will be invested in high yielding Daimler projects," Gentz said, adding such a model could be used in Asia.

Daimler, which has until now shied away from issuing debt in emerging markets so that all of its debt has more or less the same risk, said it may consider tapping these markets in the future and tempting investors with higher yields.

Brazil may be the first place such debt could be issued, Gentz said. He added that Daimler will also likely soon offer asset-backed securities in Japan, expanding the programme from Britain and the United States to Asia.
In general Daimler-Benz tries to be particularly flexible and achieve optimal financing conditions by financing in local currencies and finding the most cost-effective means of finance, Gentz said.
Next year Daimler-Benz will need to raise 15 billion marks ($9.8 billion) largely to help refinance its leasing and sales operations, Gentz said.
In 1998, Gentz predicted Daimler will need 18 billion marks ($11.8 billion) for refinancing.
